tasks.short: Create photographic recordings of geological information

steps.what: Read the actual photographic recording requirement, identify the sample or location and prepare the camera, scale and required views
inputs: Actual recording requirement and actual subject
outputs: Prepared photographic recording context

steps.what: Create the actual photographic recordings with the equipment, choosing framing, scale, lighting and views that preserve the relevant geological information
inputs: Actual sample or location and prepared camera equipment
outputs: Actual original photographs and camera metadata

steps.what: Capture and verify actual sample or location identifiers and recording context and map original photographs to those identifiers
inputs: Actual photographs, sample or location register and real capture context
outputs: Verified image-to-subject mapping and checked available metadata

steps.what: Populate the existing unsaved photographic catalogue entry with verified subject identifiers and actual embedded recording metadata according to the explicit mapping
inputs: S3 verified mapping and s2 actual embedded image metadata
outputs: Proposed photographic entry with source links and missing-metadata list

steps.what: Check the actual photographs and complete catalogue entry for legibility, correct subject, scale, recording time and metadata gaps and correct errors
inputs: Actual originals, proposed entry and verified subject mapping
outputs: Checked actual photographic record

steps.what: Save the completed photographic entry in the same existing catalogue
inputs: Checked actual photographic entry
outputs: Stored actual photographic record

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the actual camera and image-management tools, to preserve original photographs and extract actual embedded metadata into the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} photographic entry. The technician captures the images, verifies their subject mapping and checks the complete record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual image and subject metadata may be typed into catalogue fields repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Native image metadata fields or a small deterministic mapping can populate those exact fields.
tasks.still_hard: A useful photograph requires physical capture and correct geological context.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a view and scale that preserve the information being recorded.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated repeated photographic metadata entry.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: image tools can read embedded capture metadata and populate explicit catalogue fields; framing and subject verification remain human work.

assumptions: Representative actual recording episode with an existing photographic catalogue, conditional on observed manual metadata entry. No additional report or catalogue is invented. Camera metadata is produced during actual capture counted in s2; s3 counts real subject-ID, time, scale and context capture and verification. A device timestamp is not assumed accurate or equivalent to a geological location.

S4 maps image identifier, verified subject ID, checked recording time and actual available camera fields only. Missing location, scale or subject data remains manually captured and entered; no inferred geological description or free digitisation feed is assumed.

Try native image and catalogue fields first. Existing automated image recording or metadata runtime already used earns no new human saving. S4 only prepares unsaved fields, not a public image release or separate formal record commitment.

Save share1 represents negligible actual same-system time, fully retained, ungated and without author self-approval. No publication, external send or rights change is hidden in saving. Shares are illustrative task work independent of the prompt prior.
unknowns: Which metadata fields are actually typed manually?
Which actual camera fields survive the existing image workflow?

tasks.short: Measure geological characteristics for oil or gas prospecting

steps.what: Read the actual measurement plan, instrument instructions and site or borehole identifiers through native project and revision views
inputs: Actual prospecting measurement plan and existing instrument references
outputs: Verified measurement context

steps.what: Prepare actual instruments, check calibration and units and establish the real measurement location, depth and recording context
inputs: Actual instruments, site and measurement requirement
outputs: Prepared actual measurement setup and verified identifiers

steps.what: Measure the actual geological characteristics with the instruments and capture real readings with location, depth, units and time
inputs: Actual geological subject and prepared measuring instruments
outputs: Actual measurement readings and field context

steps.what: Transfer actual instrument readings into the unsaved measurement record with the explicit location, depth, time and unit mapping
inputs: Actual s3 instrument output and s2 verified recording identifiers and units
outputs: Proposed measurement record and missing-field exceptions

steps.what: Check actual original readings, depth and unit alignment and recording quality, document gaps and correct the completed measurement record
inputs: Actual originals and proposed measurement record
outputs: Checked actual measurement record with quality caveats

steps.what: Save the completed measurement record in the same existing recording system
inputs: Checked completed measurement record
outputs: Stored actual measurement record

tasks.design: Use native {OPS_SYSTEM} source views and an explicit transfer from {OTHER}, the actual geological measuring instruments, into the existing measurement form. The technician prepares and uses the instruments and checks the actual original readings and context.
tasks.previous_blocker: Where instrument outputs are retyped, the actual measurement record repeats available values.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instrument exports or a fixed field loader can prepare exact values without interpreting geology.
tasks.still_hard: Calibration, physical measurement and quality interpretation remain real field work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a bad measurement or an incorrect depth reference.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit instrument-output mappings can prepare measurement records; physical measurement and unit and depth verification remain human work.

assumptions: Representative actual measurement episode with observed retyping into an existing required record. S2 counts instrument preparation and actual location, depth and unit capture; s3 counts physical reading production. The technician and actual instrument produce the input, not a free clean feed. S4 maps location/borehole ID, depth and datum, reading value and unit, timestamp and instrument ID; missing exports or fields remain manual.

Try native instrument export and record mapping first. Automatic recording already used earns no new saving. The source-navigation reduction is only existing plan filtering, not reading technical meaning faster.

This episode uses an already permitted ordinary measuring method; separately controlled radiation sources, drilling or equipment movement are not inferred from the broad occupation description. A real episode requiring such actions must include its actual current operational authority and distinct actions.

S5 includes real quality checking and required record explanation after measurements. Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no saving or self-approval. No external report or prospecting decision is hidden. Shares are illustrative and independent of prompt time priors.
unknowns: Do the actual instruments export readings with stable depth and unit fields?

tasks.short: Participate in evaluating possible mining locations

steps.what: Collect actual candidate-location maps, sample results and access or geological constraints, verify source revisions, site identifiers, coordinates and units and define explicit comparison fields
inputs: Actual candidate-site records and original geological results
outputs: Verified site inputs, coordinate context and comparison mapping

steps.what: Assemble the explicitly mapped site comparison and calculate stated differences for comparable verified numeric fields, segregating unmatched locations, units and sampling bases
inputs: S1 verified site values, explicit comparison fields and coordinate and unit contracts
outputs: Source-linked site comparison and non-comparability exceptions

steps.what: Participate in actual site observations and technical discussion with scientists or engineers about the candidate mining locations
inputs: Actual locations, comparison and real specialist discussion
outputs: Actual site observations and clarified technical questions

steps.what: Evaluate actual geological evidence and comparison limitations and contribute technical findings about location suitability and unresolved uncertainty
inputs: Actual originals, site observations and explicit comparison exceptions
outputs: Actual technical evaluation contribution

steps.what: Write the actual existing working evaluation entry with source references, findings and unresolved comparability limits
inputs: Actual evaluation contribution and checked evidence
outputs: Actual working evaluation entry

steps.what: Save the working evaluation entry in the same document system
inputs: Completed working evaluation entry
outputs: Stored working evaluation

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the actual geological mapping and analysis application, to assemble explicitly comparable site fields from checked original records. The technician participates in field and specialist work, interprets limitations and writes the actual working contribution in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Candidate-site values may be assembled repeatedly despite explicit comparison fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed site joins and stated numeric differences can be calculated deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Sites with different sampling bases are not made comparable by matching identifiers.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what the geological evidence cannot support about a location.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated comparison assembly within existing evaluation participation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: geological analysis tools can join explicit site fields and compute specified differences while suitability evaluation remains human judgement.

assumptions: Conditional on actual repeated comparison assembly today. Geological survey and laboratory staff produce original maps and results in their normal work; s1 counts retrieving, checking coordinates, units and sampling context and mapping site fields. New surveys or tests are not a free source feed and must be counted if required.

S2 operates only on site ID, coordinate reference, checked sample basis, stated measurement and unit, explicit constraint fields and source revision. Unmatched coordinates, sampling basis or units are exceptions, not normalised by a model. Try native joins and comparison views first; existing use yields no new gain.

This is an actual technical evaluation episode with an existing working entry. Actual site observation and discussion stay in s3, actual evaluation in s4 and writing separately in s5. No board report, permit, final mining-location selection or message is invented or hidden in the save.

Ordinary same-system save share1 represents negligible actual time, fully retained and ungated. No author self-approval. Shares are unmeasured task-specific effort independent of the prompt prior; no extrapolation to an unknown mix of field and desk episodes.
unknowns: Which actual sites share a genuinely comparable sampling basis?
research_questions: Observe one real multi-site evaluation and count source preparation and non-comparability work before estimating repeated table assembly.

incremental.description: Maintain site-comparison mappings and inspect join failures beyond retained source and geological checks.

Low: differing coordinate and sampling bases leave13 of20 comparison points requiring manual reconciliation or explicit exclusion, leaving7 comparable assembly points saved;7-3=4. Source25, actual site participation20, evaluation25, entry9 and save1 remain. This is a geological comparability case, not a uniform reduction factor.

tasks.short: Assess development impacts on subsurface materials

steps.what: Collect actual development plans, subsurface observations and laboratory results, verify depths, strata, units, dates and source revisions and define the explicit impact comparisons
inputs: Actual development plans and original subsurface evidence
outputs: Verified source inputs, strata context and explicit comparison specification

steps.what: Assemble the actual baseline and development-case table and calculate explicitly specified differences for matched strata, depths, units and material characteristics
inputs: S1 verified source values and explicit comparison and unit rules
outputs: Source-linked material comparison with unmatched-stratum and missing-value exceptions

steps.what: Assess the actual environmental implications for subsurface materials against original evidence, considering pathways, uncertainty and limits of the comparison
inputs: Original subsurface evidence, actual project context and comparison exceptions
outputs: Actual impact assessment reasoning and unresolved evidence gaps

steps.what: Write the actual working assessment entry with native source-reference fields, retaining the technician's interpretation, uncertainties and limitations
inputs: Actual assessment reasoning and verified source identifiers
outputs: Actual working impact assessment with checked references

steps.what: Save the completed working assessment in the same document system
inputs: Completed actual working assessment
outputs: Stored working assessment

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the actual subsurface data and analysis tool, to assemble stated baseline and development-case comparisons from verified source values. The technician assesses actual environmental meaning and writes the working assessment in {DOCS} using checked reference fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual material comparisons and source references can require repeated table and document entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit field matching and arithmetic are deterministic; native document fields can reuse checked references.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental pathways and inadequate subsurface coverage require geological judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a numerical difference cannot support an impact conclusion.

ambition.what: Reduce demonstrated repeated assessment-table and reference work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit numeric comparisons and source-reference fields can be generated from verified subsurface inputs while environmental interpretation remains human work.

assumptions: Actual project engineers, field technicians and laboratory staff produce original plans and results in existing work. S1 counts source retrieval and actual depth, stratum, datum, unit, time and revision verification plus comparison-rule specification. New investigations, laboratory tests or scenario modelling are not free inputs; add their real work if needed.

S2 maps explicit strata and depths, measured material characteristic and unit, actual baseline/development-case source and revision, and the technician's stated difference formula. It does not predict impacts, create a development scenario or infer missing layers. Incompatible source layers stay exceptions.

Try native analysis tables and document references first. Benefit requires actual manual assembly today; existing automatic comparisons have no new runtime gain. S3 retains actual environmental reasoning and s4 retains actual writing and checking.

The actual working assessment is the task artefact, not an invented administrative report. Formal environmental submission, public release or project consent requires the actual independent final-version authority and a separate gated send; none is hidden in this save.

Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, without saving or self-approval. Shares are illustrative task-specific work, not measured or derived from prompt time priors.
